title: Overdose Deaths Climb in Laredo as DEA and Texas A&M Build Prevention Program for Kindergarteners
excerpt: Overdose deaths in Laredo rose from seven in September to 10 in October, according to police, and the DEA is partnering with Texas A&M on a first-of-its-kind bilingual drug-prevention program aimed at children as young as 5.
content:
Overdose deaths in Laredo rose from seven in September to 10 in October, a jump of more than 40 percent in a single month, according to police figures reported by KGNS on Nov. 25.

In response, the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration is partnering with Texas A&M to create a drug-prevention program aimed at children as young as 5 — something officials describe as the first of its kind in the country. The bilingual program will use cartoons and lessons to teach kindergarteners what is safe to touch and what to avoid, and it is planned to expand to parent education classes next year.

Robert Kennedy of the DEA said no one is talking to kindergarteners directly about what they should not touch, and pointed to a spike in children being exposed to drugs at home. He said he is working to protect the community’s youngest neighbors.

The new effort comes even as the DEA says fentanyl deaths in Laredo have fallen sharply since 2023, when the agency counted nearly 73 such deaths in the city. The monthly rise in October shows the danger has not gone away, and officials say reaching children early — before they are old enough to be out on their own — is the next step in prevention.

Sources: KGNS, Nov. 25, 2026, reporting by Emma Galle — “Drug prevention program for kindergarteners in development amid Laredo overdose deaths”; WiseVoter — “Laredo Overdose Deaths Rise; DEA Launches Child Prevention”, Nov. 26, 2026, https://wisevoter.com/world/us/tx/laredo/2026/11/26/laredo-overdose-deaths-rise-dea-child-prevention; KGNS — “DEA’s Fentanyl Free America campaign shows progress in Laredo”
